note: PDF pages 26-50 of the 'Verb Forms' charts booklet (Intensive Arabic Semester, Givat Haviva, (c) arabic2use). Every chart is printed LANDSCAPE (rotated 90 deg in the scan). Odd PDF pages carry content; every even PDF page (26,28,...,50) is a blank verso, several with faint pencil student vocab glosses (p026 'Invested - استثمار'; p030, p032, p034, p038, p046, p048 similar English-Arabic gloss lists) - handwriting not transcribed. Printed footer page numbers run 13-24 inside a circle; mapping: printed N = PDF page 2N+1 (p027=13 ... p049=24). Each full chart page is one verb laid out in a fixed template of boxed panels: Past tense, Past negative (both 'ma + verb' and 'ma-verb-sh' variants side by side), Present tense, Present negative (variants 'ma + b-verb' and 'b-verb-sh'), Infinitive or future tense, Negative with infinitive or future tense, Active participle and negative AP, Imperative and negative imperative, plus (on some pages) Passive Participle / Gerund / note boxes. TEACHING SEQUENCE in this chunk: Form 1 hollow (2nd radical waw, then ya, then waw-or-ya), Form 1 doubled ('dabble verb' sic, x2), Form 1 third-radical-ya (defective), then Forms 2 and 3 defective as one-line 'short conjugations', Form 4 defective, three more defective 'short conjugations' (all printed 'Form 3', apparently mislabeled - the verbs are t'ashsha/ishtara/istanna), Form 1 first-radical-waw (assimilated), Form 1 first-radical-alif, and the irregular 'to come'. The future marker rotates deliberately across pages: raH (p027), bidd- (p029), mumkin (p031), showing all three future/infinitive auxiliaries. Book misspellings preserved: 'dabble verb', 'to speek', 'To eat diner', 'liveing', 'speeking'. Scan is a low-quality photocopy: short-vowel diacritics are reproduced as best readable and may be imperfect on some prefixes; shadda/kasra clusters in 2fp/3fp negative suffixes (-tinnish/-innish) are especially hard to resolve. In negative tables below, 'ar' holds both printed variants separated by ' / '.
